phase1_leaf_result.part126_scope: One bounded 64-scenario non-destructive immutable-claim/no-wall-clock-lease model under a fixed destination-repository incarnation, using generation-scoped unique-path create for claim acquisition.
phase1_leaf_result.new_narrowing: Create-only claim acquisition is one-winner and ambiguous-create responses are recoverable by token readback, but safe takeover requires more than the immutable claim. Permanent ownership stalled all 32 abandoned-claim scenarios. Unfenced timeout takeover and split handoff/effect authority each produced 24/64 duplicate-effect traces. When generation handoff and terminal repository-local effect contended on the same current-blob-CAS authority object, safety was 64/64, takeover safety 48/48, and abandoned-claim liveness 32/32 under a later-fair-invocation assumption, without wall-clock leases.
minimal_unresolved_children: Part125 repository-incarnation write-time fencing remains orthogonal and unresolved.
Non-repository effects still require sink-side generation fencing or equivalent atomic participation.
Ambiguous success of handoff/effect CAS updates still needs stable transition/effect IDs and replay testing.

phase1_acceptance.accepted_scope: repository-local effect state only, fixed destination-repository incarnation, cooperative crash/retry agents, same-authority-file CAS generation fencing
phase1_acceptance.scope_guard: This is not generic GitHub-service impossibility/possibility, not repository-rebind safety, not Byzantine safety, and not proof for external side-effect sinks.

continuation: Part127: execute one bounded ambiguous-CAS replay model for the Part126 same-authority generation state machine under the same fixed-destination-incarnation scope. Inject response loss after a successful generation-advance CAS and after a successful terminal-effect CAS, plus a concurrent third invocation and a rate-limit interruption before readback. Require stable transition_id/effect_id, monotonic generation, current-blob CAS, and exact readback to distinguish already-applied from not-applied writes. Test whether any trace can double-advance, resurrect an old claimant, or duplicate terminal effect; keep repository-incarnation write-time fencing and non-repository sink fencing as orthogonal unresolved children.
